tasks.title: Server delivery-time aggregation surface
tasks.description: Add a project-scoped read surface `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/delivery-time` returning one entry per delivered issue (completion date, lead time, cycle time) over a fixed 30-day trailing window keyed on completion time. Implement `IssueQuerier.GetDeliveryTimesAsync(projectId, now)` reading lead time from `Issue.CreatedAt`, cycle time from the earliest `work-started` event, and the completion anchor from `Issue.CompletedAt` — applying the first-work-start-to-final-completion rule for retries and excluding cancelled issues. Add the `DeliveryTimeResult`/`DeliveryTimePoint` internal records, the `DeliveryTimeMetricsResponse`/`DeliveryTimePointDto` wire DTOs, and the `MapIssueDeliveryTimeMetrics` route partial registered in `IssueRoutes.cs`. The surface is strictly additive: existing `/metrics/completion`, `/metrics/quality`, `/metrics/approval-wait` are untouched. Zero delivered issues returns `200` with empty `Points`; unknown project returns `404`.
acceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/delivery-time` returns `200` with one `DeliveryTimePointDto` per delivered issue completed within `[now - 30d, now]`, each carrying `IssueNumber`, ISO-8601 `CompletedAt`, `LeadDays`, and nullable `CycleDays`.
Lead time equals `CompletedAt - CreatedAt` for every delivered issue; cycle time equals `CompletedAt - earliest(work-started event time)`, retaining the earliest work-start across retries.
A reopened-and-re-completed issue is anchored at its latest `CompletedAt` while preserving the earliest work-start; the prior completion is not retained as a separate sample.
A delivered issue with no recorded `IssueWorkStarted` carries `CycleDays == null` (undefined), distinguishable from a genuine zero-duration cycle (`CycleDays == 0`); `LeadDays` is always defined.
Cancelled issues do not contribute a sample; only issues with `Status == Done` and non-null `CompletedAt` are included.
A project with zero delivered issues in the window returns `200` with an empty `Points` array (not an error, not a fabricated zero).
An unknown project reference returns `404`.
The existing completion/quality/approval-wait metrics endpoints remain available and unchanged.
`now` is an injected `DateTimeOffset` parameter (no `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` inside the method), satisfying the no-wall-clock testing rule.

Unit tests in `IssueQuerierSpecs.cs` cover lead/cycle computation, retry-keeps-earliest-start, reopen-moves-completion-anchor, no-work-start→null cycle, cancelled-excluded, 30-day windowing, and empty window; HTTP specs in `IssueMetricsApiSpecs.cs` cover the `200`/`404`/empty/shape cases. `npm test` passes (C# warnings-as-errors).
tasks.output: packages/server IssueQuerier.GetDeliveryTimesAsync + DTOs + route partial + unit/HTTP specs, verified by `npm test`
tasks.notes: Pure additive read over already-persisted lifecycle events — no new events, no schema change, no domain writes. Reuse existing SeedIssue/SeedEvent test helpers and the IssueEvents work-started scan idiom from GetQualityAsync (Min instead of latest). Deploy via `mo update server`.

tasks.title: Web cycle-time scatter control chart widget
tasks.description: Add a cycle-time scatter control chart to the Dashboard Productivity zone consuming the delivery-time surface from T-001. Build three composable pieces: (1) a `useDeliveryTime` hook under `entities/issue/api/delivery-time.ts` mirroring `completion-trend.ts`; (2) a new `ScatterSeries` kit primitive under `pages/dashboard/charts/` rendering one `<circle>` per point with `transform`/`opacity`-only motion; (3) a pure `computeRollingPercentile(samples, window, p)` helper under `pages/dashboard/productivity/model/delivery-time.ts`. Assemble these into `CycleTimeChart.tsx`: one scatter point per delivered issue positioned by completion date (x) and duration in days (y), a client-side lead-time/cycle-time lens toggle (cycle lens excludes null-cycle issues), and overlaid rolling P50 (median, nearest-rank) and P85 (linear-interpolation) percentile lines over a fixed 10-issue trailing window that plots from the first valid sample. Mount in `ProductivityZone.tsx`. Route loading/error/empty through the shared `ChartContainer`; the empty state names a concrete next action. Legend distinguishes scatter/P50/P85 by shape (dot/solid/dashed), not color alone.
acceptanceCriteria: `CycleTimeChart` renders in the Productivity zone with one scatter point per delivered issue, x-positioned by completion date and y-positioned by duration in fractional days.

A lead-time/cycle-time lens toggle switches scatter y-values and percentile overlays; selecting the cycle lens excludes issues with undefined `CycleDays` from both scatter and percentile recomputation.

P50 and P85 rolling percentile lines overlay the scatter, computed client-side from the per-issue series over a fixed 10-issue trailing window; lines plot from the first valid sample even when the window is not yet full.

`computeRollingPercentile` uses nearest-rank for P50 (median) and linear-interpolation for P85; unit tests in `model/delivery-time.test.ts` cover partial leading window, null-exclusion per lens, and even-sample interpolation deterministically.

`ScatterSeries` renders one `<circle>` per point with `transform`/`opacity`-only motion honoring `useReducedMotion`; co-located `.test.ts` covers rendering; existing chart kit primitives (`BarSeries`/`LineSeries`/`SegmentedBarSeries`) are untouched (zero regression).

Loading, error, and empty states route through the shared `ChartContainer`; the empty state names a concrete next action (cycle time appears once an issue completes on the project); no bare empty coordinate axis is rendered.
The legend disambiguates scatter series, P50 line, and P85 line by shape (dot vs solid vs dashed), satisfying the non-color-only accessibility requirement.

The widget composes against the pinned chart library, `--chart-*` theme tokens, the accessibility wrapper (SR data summary), `tabular-nums`, and `transform`/`opacity`-only motion; no new charting library dependency is introduced.
Scatter x-position is driven by `CompletedAt` only; a post-completion edit bumping `updatedAt` does not move/add/resurface a point.

`ProductivityZone.test.tsx` includes the delivery-time mock and chart ordering assertion; any dashboard-page test mocking `entities/issue` includes `useDeliveryTime`. `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: packages/web useDeliveryTime hook + ScatterSeries primitive + model/delivery-time.ts helper + CycleTimeChart.tsx + ProductivityZone mount + tests, verified by `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web`
tasks.notes: The widget is purely read-only — no domain writes. Durations are fractional days (double) preserving sub-day vertical spread; display formatted to 1 decimal. Rolling window N=10 is a fixed constant behind the helper (not user-configurable). Single left y-axis (days) for scatter, P50, and P85.
